glossary.fixedCharge.def: What you pay each month just for being connected, even with zero consumption.
glossary.igv.def: Tax added at the end, on energy plus the fixed charge. You can turn it off here to see the net amount.
glossary.lighting.def: Share for street lights. Separate from your consumption and usually a small part of the bill.
glossary.kwh.def: One kilowatt-hour: running something at 1000 W for one hour.

explainer.title: From kWh to soles, step by step
explainer.intro: The calculator doesn't guess: it applies, in order, your tariff price, fixed charges, IGV tax and the billing period. This is exactly what it does, using the numbers of the verified BT5B residential tariff.
explainer.step1.title: 1 · Energy
explainer.step1.body: We multiply your consumption in kWh by your tariff's price per kWh. It's the only component that depends on how much you consume.
explainer.step2.title: 2 · Fixed charge
explainer.step2.body: We add the fixed charge if its switch is on. It pays for being connected to the grid, whether you consume or not.
explainer.step3.title: 3 · Public lighting
explainer.step3.body: We add public lighting if it's on. It's the contribution for street lights, independent of your consumption.
explainer.step4.title: 4 · Subtotal without IGV
explainer.step4.body: We add energy plus charges. Everything below is computed on this subtotal.
explainer.step5.title: 5 · IGV 18%
explainer.step5.body: We apply the tax on the whole subtotal: energy and charges pay IGV equally. If you turn it off, the total stays at the subtotal.
explainer.step6.title: 6 · Period
explainer.step6.body: On a monthly period everything stays as is. On bimonthly, every component is multiplied by 2 before totaling.
explainer.inverse.title: Backwards: from soles to kWh
explainer.inverse.body: To estimate consumption from an amount, we undo the steps in reverse: first divide by 1 plus the IGV, then subtract the charges, and finally divide by the price. The order matters: IGV is undone before subtracting charges, because on the way in it taxes the whole subtotal. If the price is 0, or the amount doesn't even cover the charges with their IGV, the result is 0 kWh.
explainer.inverse.caption: The example total, converted back
explainer.toggles.title: The switches
explainer.toggles.body: Fixed charge, lighting and IGV each have a switch in settings: turning one off removes that component from the calculation (it counts as 0). A monthly period multiplies by 1 and a bimonthly one by 2.

explainer.note.title: Reference prices
explainer.note.body: Prices are approximate and editable: only the BT5B residential tariff is verified against a real bill (Lima Norte, June 2026). The rest are estimates that may differ from OSINERGMIN's current tariff schedule.
